decision: Owner 2026-09-22: fix the labTune Bo fallback in the engine (engines #235); lead decision 2026-09-22, Option A: the fluid course follows the fixed engine. fluid advanced: RE-KEY the six W5b tuned values in place onto what the fixed engine gives on the same case.

why: The W5b case (Good Oil Co. Well No. 4 tuned against its 200 psig separator test) is unchanged. The engine's labTune Bo fallback, used whenever the model is two phase at the lab reservoir conditions, re-scanned without the saturation-pressure window and stepped 1e-6 relative above a boundary bisected only to 0.05 psia, so it returned a null Bo at random and the regression met its penalty residual. With the fallback fixed (engines #235) the same regression converges in 16 iterations (was 59) to a lower residual, and all six tuned values move by more than their tolerances. Each keeps its key, label, unit and tolerance and takes the fixed engine's value; the prompt does not move.

good_oil_tuned_bo_rb_stb.evidence: HD re-key (engines #235, 20261030d_hd_fluid.sql): same key, label, unit and tol; expected 1.4621628562343378 -> 1.4729609026685642. The labTune Bo fallback had returned a null Bo at random during the regression, so the fit met its penalty residual and the W5b key was an artefact of it. The new value is goodOilTuned(2) on the vendored engine, the regression the tuning explorer runs when the learner chooses the 200 psig test (hd/fluid/keys.mjs; panelCapstoneGuard.test.js). W5b's case evidence stands: The lessons printed every answer and the tuning explorer opened on the 100 psig regression. Re-cased on the regression against the 200 psig test; the tuned saturation pressure becomes the tuned Bo, because any regression lands the saturation pressure within a fraction of a psi of the 2634.65 target it fits, which is the teaching answer too.
